title: O, Speak That Gracious Word Again
description: O, Speak That Gracious Word Again in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 53, “Peace restored”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, speak that gra-cious word a-gain, And cheer my droop-ing heart! No voice but thine can soothe my pain, Or bid my fears de-part.

lines: O, speak that gracious word again,
And cheer my drooping heart!
No voice but thine can soothe my pain,
Or bid my fears depart.
And canst thou still vouchsafe to own
A wretch so vile as I?
And may I still approach thy throne,
And Abba, Father, cry?
Oh then let saints and angels join,
And help me to proclaim,
The grace that healed a breach like mine,
And put my foes to shame!
How oft did Satan's cruel boast
My troubled soul affright!
He told me I was surely lost,
And God had left me quite.
Guilt made me fear, lest all were true
The lying tempter said!
But now the Lord appears in view,
My enemy is fled.
My Savior, by his pow'rful word,
Has turned my night to day;
And his salvation's joys restored,
Which I had sinned away.
Dear Lord I wonder and adore,
Thy grace is all divine;
Oh keep me, that I sin no more
Against such love as thine!

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
